title: Security
purpose: When an account gets taken over, a wave of chargebacks lands or last week's traffic looks too good to be true, open Security to see what happened, what it costs and what to lock down first.
fires: the developer called at midnight, the processor's warning email read too late, the help-page search during a hijack, and the habit of assuming a small store is not a target.
not_for: a brand that wants a full security audit or a penetration test; this finds and ranks the money risks, it does not replace a security firm.

jobs.job: When my Meta ad account is suddenly spending on ads I did not make, help me lock it, stop the spend and get it back, so I do not lose thousands and weeks of selling
jobs.circumstance: Saturday morning, a card alert for $4,000 in ad spend overnight, unknown ads for another product are live, the admin list has a stranger on it, Meta support is a form

progress.functional: know who got in, what they changed, what it cost, and the steps to lock and recover
progress.emotional: stop the panic of watching money drain with no one to call
progress.social: tell a partner and the agency what happened and that it is handled

jobs.hire_today: the agency's contact at Meta if there is one, a freelancer who knows the recovery forms, forum threads, or nothing
jobs.fire: the frantic search through help pages and the habit of sharing one login across the agency

forces.push: money leaves every hour and the account may be lost for weeks
forces.pull: a first-hour checklist with the exact steps, contacts and evidence to send
forces.anxiety: what if I lock myself out or make recovery slower

jobs.little_hire: the hour a hijack is suspected, then weekly on who has access

watch.metric: unapproved ad spend and unknown admins on ad accounts, daily
watch.source: Meta Business settings and card or billing alerts

drives.metric: days of ad account downtime per year

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,000 spent by a hijacker and 11 days without ads. After: spend stopped within 1 hour, access back in 2 days, 0 unknown admins since.
jobs.not_for: a brand that does not run paid ads on any platform

jobs.job: When I hear another founder lost their ad account and store to one phishing link, tell me which of our logins could be taken the same way and fix them this week, so it does not happen to us
jobs.circumstance: a founder group chat, a story of a hijacked account and a store emptied, the founder realises nobody has checked our logins

progress.functional: know which admin logins on store, ads, email, bank and domain lack two-step login or are shared
progress.emotional: stop the low hum of worry that we are next
progress.social: tell the team and partner we are covered, and mean it

jobs.hire_today: nothing, because it feels like a big-company problem
jobs.fire: the shared passwords in a doc and the habit of assuming a small store is not a target

forces.push: one stolen login can empty an ad account or change payout details
forces.pull: a short list of weak logins with a fix for each, done in a week
forces.anxiety: what if two-step login locks out the agency or slows the team

jobs.little_hire: once a quarter, and when anyone joins or leaves

watch.metric: admin logins across store, ads, email, bank and domain with two-step login on, weekly
watch.source: admin access lists from Shopify, Meta, Google, email tool, bank and registrar

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 of 22 admin logins have no two-step login, 3 are shared. After: 22 of 22 protected, 0 shared, within 7 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand where one person holds every login and already uses a security key on each

forces.push: past the line, payouts get held or the account closes
forces.pull: the rate, the cause and the fix in one view, with a reply ready for the processor
forces.habit: we answer disputes when they arrive
forces.anxiety: what if the fix blocks good customers

watch.metric: disputes as a share of orders, trailing 30 days, against the processor's warning line
watch.source: Shopify Payments, Stripe or PayPal dispute reports

drives.metric: payout amount held by the processor

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: dispute rate 0.9 percent against a 1 percent line, a warning received. After: card testing blocked and descriptor fixed, rate at 0.3 percent in 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand with very few card payments
